newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-VOGTS HOPING FOR HIGH-SCORING EXHIBITION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VOGTS HOPING FOR HIGH-SCORING EXHIBITION.

text.p: Berti Vogts, the coach of the European side playing Africa in an exhibition All Star match on Wednesday night, said he expected the game to be an open one full of attacking soccer.
"It is a friendly game, the result does not matter and I am sending my team out to look for goals," the German international manager said.
"It will be fascinating to see the contrast between the European and African styles of playing.
"It does not matter who wins and I am intending to play three at the back, with the emphasis on attack for the midfielders and the front men."
The same mood was reflected in the African camp.

Ismail Bhamjee of Botswana, an executive committee member of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), said: "Wednesday's match is very important for a number of symbolic reasons, but the result is not important. Our team will also be going for goals and I am looking forward to an open game."
The match is the first ever between representative sides from Europe and Africa and kicks off the European Union's Year Against Racism.
An under-17 tournament involving France, Greece, Portugal and Spain from Europe and Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast and Nigeria from Africa starts on Friday and continues until February 9.
"The wider message of course is that football has a big role to play in combating racism," added Vogts.

"I am very happy to be associated with this initiative because racism is still a problem in many parts of Europe and if this can help break it down, then that is very good. Perhaps we can have these matches once or twice a year."

Although the match is billed as an All Star game and does include top names like German Juergen Klinsmann, Croatian Zvonimir Boban, the Dutch twins Frank and Ronald de Boer and Ghana's Abedi Pele, club commitments mean many other players are absent.
The English premier league, for example, has a full programme on Wednesday night which ruled out not only all the English players but also all the dozens of overseas players now based in England.
Vogts was optimistic however that his German compatriot Matthias Sammer would play in the match. Sammer has been appointed as the European skipper but was not due in Lisbon until later on Wednesday.

Bhamjee added: "If we do have other matches in the future then we will have to look again at the time of year they are played. It is a shame so many top players cannot be here, but there is still plenty of talent on display."
The match is the 53rd such "All Star" game since the first one of its type was played between a Central European XI and Western European Select in Amsterdam in 1937.
Many have been high scoring, and only one has ended goalless when Africa drew 0-0 with CONCACAF in a match in Brazil in 1972.
